response.title: which portable power station is best for a week of camping with a fridge
response.answer:
For a week of camping with an electric fridge, I'd recommend a portable power station with at least 2,000Wh of battery capacity, preferably paired with a 200–400W solar panel.

My top choices would be from EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX, and Bluetti. The best one depends on whether you'll have solar charging and how much electricity your fridge consumes.

How much power do you need for 7 days?

A typical 12V camping compressor fridge uses around 300–600Wh per day, depending on its size, ambient temperature, insulation, and thermostat setting.

Fridge consumption

	

7-day energy requirement




Efficient, 300Wh/day

	

2,100Wh




Typical, 450Wh/day

	

3,150Wh




High, 600Wh/day

	

4,200Wh

These are estimates before additional conversion losses.

A 2,000Wh station usually won't last seven days without recharging. But with reliable solar charging, it can be a very practical setup.

Best overall

Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station - 2,048Wh | 2…

2,048Wh · 41.7 lb · 800W max solar

Excellent for camping because of its relatively low standby consumption, manageable weight, and expandable battery.

$1,499.00 at Anker-US

EcoFlow Battery Generator DELTA 2 Max Solar Generator, 2400W…

2,048Wh · ~53 lb · 1,000W max solar

Best alternative if you want higher solar input and room to expand to approximately 6kWh.

$1,049.00 at The Home Depot

Anker SOLIX C2000X Gen 2 with 200W solar panel

2,048Wh · Includes 200W solar panel

A convenient ready-to-go package, although I'd prefer 400W of solar for a weeklong trip.

$1,199.99 at Lowe's

What I would buy

Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 + 400W solar panel for a typical 12V compressor fridge. It offers a good balance of battery capacity, efficiency, and portability. Its official specifications confirm 2,048Wh capacity and 800W maximum solar input. 
Anker SOLIX US
+1

With 400W of solar, you might harvest roughly 800–1,400Wh on a reasonably sunny day, depending on weather, shade, and panel positioning. That should generally cover a 300–600Wh/day fridge with some margin, but several cloudy days could still be a problem.

One important tip: connect a 12V fridge directly to the station's DC output when compatible. This avoids leaving the AC inverter running continuously and can improve runtime.

Two questions that would change my recommendation
What kind of fridge will you use?
12V camping fridge (Dometic, ICECO, BougeRV, etc.)
Regular 120V mini fridge

Will you be able to recharge during the week?
Yes, using solar panels
No, battery only for all 7 days
Yes, from my vehicle

These two details make a big difference: you might need only a 1–2kWh station with solar, or 4–6kWh of battery capacity for a full week without recharging.
